expectations.text: Rejects a willingness-to-pay survey method such as Van Westendorp or MaxDiff as unworkable at one event's sponsor-pool size
expectations.evidence: "Van Westendorp and MaxDiff 'need hundreds of prospective buyers'. A sponsor base is dozens at most."

expectations.text: Names comparable events' published rate cards as the practical substitute for willingness-to-pay research
expectations.evidence: "Give the board market comps instead ... practical substitute for willingness-to-pay research."

expectations.text: Sequences the methods as cost-recovery for the total, market-comp to band each tier, value-based to allocate within the band
expectations.evidence: "cost-recovery fixes the total, market comps set the band for each tier, and value-based work allocates inside the band."

expectations.text: States that cost-recovery needs the budget's expense total and sponsorship share before any tier is priced
expectations.evidence: "Sum the expense lines ... and multiply by the sponsorship share."

expectations.text: Prices the AI track exclusivity at a multiple above the top general tier rather than at add-on money
expectations.evidence: Rejects the multiple: "The reference data doesn't back that up ... about 0.5x ... So price it by value-based reasoning, not by a multiple."

expectations.text: Puts a hard cap on the number of exclusivity slots sold
expectations.evidence: "Cap the count, and decide up front whether it is per-event or series-wide."

expectations.text: Confirms exclusivity is sellable here because the series sits at the vendor or foundation pole
expectations.evidence: "You're vendor-backed, so selling exclusivity is allowed."

expectations.text: Prices the three-event bundle as a small fixed published discount step in the single-digit percent range, scaling with the number of events signed
expectations.evidence: "3% for one event, 5% for two signed together, 8% for three or more"; "Publish the bundle rule".

expectations.text: States that bundling requires real portfolio contract mechanics to honour, and that this is why it is promoted here
expectations.evidence: Says "Your portfolio is real" but gives no contract-mechanics rationale.

expectations.text: Promotes value-based pricing for the AI track because no comparable event publishes a price for that inventory
expectations.evidence: "because no comparable event publishes a price you can lean on."

expectations.text: Does not list track exclusivity as an add-on beside surfaces like coffee or lanyards
expectations.evidence: Exclusivity is treated as a separate section, "AI-track exclusivity: put it on the card".

expectations.text: Does not offer an open-ended or negotiated discount in exchange for the three-event commitment
expectations.evidence: "Bundle only simultaneous signings, with the rate fixed and written. No off-card deals."
